curriculum: English-taught full-time Maastricht Global Studies starts in September. The 2026–27 regulations list four 30 EC semesters followed by 25 EC Peace & Justice with field study, a 20 EC thesis or alternative final work, and 15 EC 21st Century Learning. The selected route uses the listed Peace & Justice course sequence and interdisciplinary thesis. A 25 EC minor replaces the Peace & Justice content, skills and field study, with a literature exam of up to 12 EC for an approved minor shortfall. The four language classes are 3 EC each. English and native languages are excluded, and the required proficiency must be reached. Appendix 2 explicitly changes GLO2641 to Researching Tolerance & Beliefs, resolving the earlier catalogue title.
progression: Course years follow chronological order under Article 4.2. Tutorials normally require 83 percent attendance and some skills modules require full attendance under Article 4.4. The first four semesters combine two theme courses, two methods courses, two skills courses, a 4 EC project and the language classes. The 20 EC final work spans periods 3 through 5 in Year 3 and overlaps 21st Century Learning in periods 4 and 5. The standard thesis addresses a globalisation-related topic through at least two disciplines.
